_note: Source of truth for MCP tool descriptions (TDQS standard, /workspace/promo/tdqs-standard.md). scripts/build_catalog.py writes these over the Apify Store text; catalog.py appends the generated Behavior/price/run-control paragraph. Do not restate schema fields here.
reference_checker: Verify an existing bibliography against Crossref: flags fake (AI-hallucinated), miscited and retracted references, one row per reference. Unlike citation_formatter, it judges whether a reference is real and accurate; it does not produce formatted styles. Use when you must audit a reference list, DOIs or titles before submission or review. Do not use to discover new papers (use literature_search or pubmed_evidence_table) or to restyle citations (use citation_formatter). Parameters: give bibliography, dois or titles (at least one). Lowering minMatchScore finds more but risks false matches; includeCandidates adds audit detail without extra charge. mode=monitor re-checks the DOIs/ORCID works against the state saved under monitorName and reports only new problems, so reuse the same monitorName on scheduled runs. Each reference checked is billed, so maxReferences/run_max_items cap cost on long lists. Returns per item: summary, status (OK/CHECK/FIX), verdict, matchedDoi, matchScore, mismatches (cited vs actual), integrity.status (retracted, corrected, expression-of-concern), openAccessUrl, warnings.
citation_formatter: Convert DOIs, ISBNs, PMIDs, arXiv IDs, titles or messy reference strings into checked citations in APA 7, MLA 9, Chicago, Harvard, IEEE, Vancouver, BibTeX and RIS. Unlike reference_checker, it formats rather than audits: unresolved items are listed, not diagnosed as fake or retracted. Use when you need a clean bibliography or .bib/.ris export. Do not use to find papers (use literature_search) or to prove references are genuine (use reference_checker first). Parameters: pass references (one per line) or paste a whole list or .bib/.ris contents in text. All styles are one price, so request every style you might need in one call rather than calling again. Text lookups below minMatchScore stay unresolved; DOIs and IDs resolve exactly. Only formatted citations are billed. Returns per item: summary, status, one field per style (apa, mla, ...), inText, bibtex, ris, doi, title, authors, year, containerTitle; combined bibliography files stay in the run's Apify key-value store.
literature_search: Search 250M+ scholarly works (OpenAlex) by topic query or seed DOIs and return ranked papers with DOI, citation count, free PDF link, retraction flag and a ready citation. Unlike pubmed_evidence_table (PubMed biomedical records with study design and PRISMA counts), this covers every discipline and supports citation-network expansion. Use when you need real papers on a topic, a reading list, or papers citing/cited by known DOIs. Do not use for systematic biomedical screening (use pubmed_evidence_table) or to find people (use researcher_expert_finder). Parameters: seedDois with no query walks the citation network per seedMode (citing = forward, references = backward); with a query it searches inside that network. searchIn=fullText broadens recall but lowers precision. retractedPapers=flag returns and bills retracted papers marked FIX; exclude drops them unbilled. sortBy changes dataset order only; readingListSize does not affect cost. Returns per item: summary, status, title, authors, year, venue, doi, citations, readingRank, readingScore, isOpenAccess, pdfUrl, retracted, citation, bibtex, ris, abstract.
pubmed_evidence_table: Run one or more PubMed queries and return a screening-ready evidence table: one row per article with PMID, journal, study design, sample size, retraction status and citation, plus PRISMA-style counts for the whole search. Unlike literature_search (all disciplines, OpenAlex ranking, citation-network walks), this uses native PubMed syntax and MeSH and is built for systematic-review screening. Use when the question is biomedical/clinical and you need reproducible PubMed queries or design filters (RCT, meta-analysis, cohort). Do not use for non-biomedical topics (use literature_search), for trial registrations (use clinical_trial_leads) or to verify a reference list (use reference_checker). Parameters: queries accept PubMed field tags ([tiab], [mh], [pt]) and Boolean operators; several queries are de-duplicated into one table. Filters (studyDesigns, excludeAnimalOnly, hasAbstract, freeFullTextOnly, excludePreprints) run before billing, and PRISMA counts still report what they removed. retractedArticles=flag bills retracted rows marked FIX; exclude drops them unbilled. sampleSize is parsed from the abstract and comes with sampleSizeConfidence; treat low confidence as unverified. Returns per item: summary, status, pmid, title, year, journal, studyDesign, sampleSize, sampleSizeConfidence, retractionStatus, retracted, citation. Excel, PRISMA and RIS/Rayyan import files stay in the run's Apify key-value store.
researcher_expert_finder: Rank the academic experts and key opinion leaders on a research topic from OpenAlex, with institution, ORCID, h-index, topic paper counts and their recent topic papers. Unlike literature_search (returns papers) this returns people; unlike company_team_finder (staff listed on a company website) it covers academics by publication record. Use when you need reviewers, KOLs, collaborators or speakers for a topic, optionally by country or institution. Do not use for company contacts (use company_team_finder) or for papers themselves (use literature_search). Parameters: the ranked pool is the 200 authors with the most matching papers, so maxResults above 200 adds nothing. maxAuthorsPerPaper ignores mega-collaboration papers that would inflate everyone on them; raise it only for physics-style fields. yearFrom/yearTo limit which papers count, while activeSince filters people. includeOrcid adds employment and bio at no extra charge. Returns per item: expert score, name, ORCID, current institution and country, h-index, total and topic works/citations, recent topic papers (title, year, DOI, citations), summary.
pdf_table_extractor: Extract every table from PDF files (by URL or from an Apify key-value store) into structured rows, Excel and CSV, with optional OCR for scanned pages. Unlike sec_financials_excel (standardized XBRL financials straight from SEC filings), this reads whatever tables a PDF contains. Use when the data you need is locked in PDF tables: reports, statements, government releases. Do not use for SEC-listed company financials (use sec_financials_excel, which is exact) or to find papers (use literature_search). Parameters: billing is per page analysed plus per table extracted, so pages and maxPagesPerPdf are the real cost levers; run_max_items does not cap pages. ocrScannedPages=false skips and lists scanned pages; turning it on adds the per-OCR-page price up to maxOcrPagesPerPdf, and is much slower. detection=auto tries ruled-grid then whitespace detection; force lattice or stream only if auto merges or splits columns. Files over 150 MB fail and are not charged. Returns per item (one per table): summary, pages, header, row and column counts and cell data; Excel/CSV files stay in the run's Apify key-value store.
npi_provider_lists: Build de-duplicated lists of US healthcare providers (individuals and organizations) from the official CMS NPI Registry by specialty and territory, with NPI, name, specialty, practice address and phone. Unlike clinical_trial_leads (trial sites and investigators) or local_business_leads (any business category from OpenStreetMap), this is the authoritative US provider registry. Use when you need doctors, dentists, therapists, pharmacies or clinics in states, cities or ZIPs. Do not use for non-US providers or for email addresses (NPI publishes none; follow up with company_website_enricher on practice domains). Parameters: specialties take plain words, mapped to NPI taxonomies. Large states are split by ZIP automatically, so you are not limited by the registry's 1,200-result ceiling. cities and zipCodes narrow the states given. maxResults is shared across all specialty x area combinations. primarySpecialtyOnly=true removes providers who list the specialty only as secondary; includeSecondaryLocations=false drops providers whose main office is outside the territory. Returns per item: summary, NPI, provider type, name, specialty/taxonomy, practice address, phone.
grants_finder: Search US federal funding in one call: open and forecasted Grants.gov opportunities plus already-funded NIH RePORTER and NSF awards, one row per grant with agency, dates, amount (USD), eligibility and link. Unlike sbir_sttr_topic_radar (SBIR/STTR solicitation topics with deadlines and DoD Q&A) and federal_contract_finder (procurement contracts on USAspending), this covers assistance grants and research awards. Use when you need grants to apply for or want to see who was funded for a topic. Do not use for contracts (use federal_contract_finder) or small-business R&D topics (use sbir_sttr_topic_radar). Parameters: sources picks the mix; grants_gov is apply-able funding, nih/nsf are past awards. maxResultsPerSource applies to each source, so worst-case billed rows = maxResultsPerSource x number of sources; run_max_items does not set it, so keep it small first and rely on run_max_charge_usd. minAmount drops rows whose source publishes no amount. includeGrantsGovDetails adds award ceiling and eligibility but slows the run; turn it off for quick scans. Returns per item: agentSummary, source, recordType, status, title, agency, number, openDate, closeDate, amount, eligibility, summary, url.
federal_contract_finder: Find US federal prime contract awards on USAspending.gov by keyword, NAICS, PSC, agency, place of performance, set-aside or recipient, or switch to recompete mode to list contracts whose period of performance ends soon. Unlike grants_finder (assistance grants and research awards) and sbir_sttr_topic_radar (open SBIR/STTR topics), this returns procurement contracts with incumbent, UEI and end date. Use when you need incumbents, competitor contract history, market sizing by NAICS/agency, or recompete pipeline leads. Do not use for grants (use grants_finder) or for open solicitations you can bid on today (USAspending holds awards, not SAM.gov notices). Parameters: mode=awards honors sortBy and dateFrom/dateTo (activity window, default last 24 months); mode=recompete ignores sortBy, sorts by soonest end date and uses recompeteMonths as the window. NAICS prefixes cover all child codes. recipientNames accepts company names or UEIs for competitor lookups. Keywords under 3 characters are rejected. Returns per item: agentSummary, awardId, recipientName, recipientUei, amount, awardingAgency, awardingSubAgency, naicsCode, pscCode, description, startDate, endDate, monthsLeft, status, performanceState, url.
email_domain_security_checker: Audit email authentication for a list of domains: SPF, DKIM (about 40 common selectors), DMARC, MX provider, MTA-STS, TLS-RPT and BIMI, graded A-F with spoofing risk and plain-English fixes. Unlike company_website_enricher (firmographics, tech stack, contacts), this only grades mail security posture from public DNS. Use when you need deliverability or spoofing checks, a security prospect list, or a vendor review. Do not use for website SEO or AI-readiness (use ai_search_seo_audit) or for page-level prompt injection (use hidden_ai_instructions_scanner). Parameters: domains accept bare domains, emails or URLs and are normalized and de-duplicated. DKIM is only confirmed when a selector matches; add dkimSelectors you know are in use, otherwise a missing DKIM may be a false negative. Nonexistent or unresolvable domains are returned with a status and not charged. Returns per item: agentSummary, domain, grade, score (0-100), spoofable, mailProvider, spfRecord, spfAll, spfLookups, dmarcRecord, dmarcPolicy, dmarcReporting, dkimSelectorsFound, mtaSts, tlsRpt, bimi, mxHosts, fixes (prioritized), status.
ai_search_seo_audit: Audit web pages for classic SEO and for AI-search readiness (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Google AI Overviews): titles, meta, schema/FAQ markup, author/date signals, blocked AI crawlers, llms.txt and ranked fixes, with an SEO score and an AI-readiness score per page. Unlike website_change_monitor (diffs pages over time) and hidden_ai_instructions_scanner (finds concealed prompt-injection text), this grades how discoverable and citable a page is. Use when you need an on-page SEO/GEO audit or an llms.txt draft. Do not use for change tracking (use website_change_monitor) or security scanning (use hidden_ai_instructions_scanner or email_domain_security_checker). Parameters: crawlInternalLinks multiplies pages: each URL can add up to that many same-site pages, and every page is billed, so maxPages/run_max_items is the real cost cap. generateLlmsTxt drafts one llms.txt per site lacking it at no extra charge. Pages that block our crawler are returned unbilled. Returns per item: agentSummary, url, seoScore, aiReadinessScore, title, metaDescription, h1, wordCount, schemaTypes, faqSchema, aiSearchBotsBlocked, aiTrainingBotsBlocked, llmsTxt, sitemapFound, canonical, noindex, crawlerBlocked, fixes.
podcast_leads_finder: Find active podcasts to pitch by topic from Apple Podcasts and each show's public RSS feed: host, contact email published in the feed, website, socials, episode count, last episode date and a guest-friendly signal. Unlike local_business_leads or company_team_finder (businesses and staff), this targets shows and their hosts for guest booking or sponsorship outreach. Use when you need a podcast guesting, PR or sponsorship list for a niche. Do not use for audience or download numbers (not public) or for general topic popularity (use topic_trends_tracker). Parameters: each keyword is searched separately and results are de-duplicated; deepSearch=true (default) searches descriptions too for up to 3x more shows but is slower. onlyWithEmail and guestFriendlyOnly filter before billing, so they shrink both list and cost. activeWithinDays=0 includes dormant shows. Emails come only from RSS feeds; nothing is guessed. Returns per item: agentSummary, podcastName, author, email, emailSource, website, socials, appleUrl, feedUrl, primaryGenre, episodeCount, lastEpisodeDate, avgDaysBetweenEpisodes, guestFriendly, guestEpisodeShare, recentEpisodeTitles.
local_business_leads: List local businesses by category and place (city, county, ZIP, neighborhood or lat/lon radius) from OpenStreetMap under its open license, with address, phone, email, website, opening hours and socials. Unlike npi_provider_lists (official US healthcare registry) or trucking_company_leads (FMCSA carriers), this covers any business type worldwide, with coverage as good as local OSM mapping. Use when you need a prospect list such as plumbers in Phoenix or cafes in a ZIP. Do not use for US healthcare providers (use npi_provider_lists, which is authoritative) or for reviews/ratings (OSM has none). Parameters: give location, or latitude+longitude (radiusKm defaults to 5); radiusKm with a location searches a circle instead of the official boundary. Whole states or countries are slow, often longer than 60 s, so raise run_timeout_secs to 300 or narrow the area. requireEmail sharply reduces results because few OSM entries list email. Returns per item: agentSummary, name, category, street, city, state, postcode, phone, email, website, openingHours, socials, lat, lon, osmUrl, attribution (ODbL; credit OpenStreetMap when you republish).
company_hiring_signals: Measure hiring intent per company from its public job board (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby and more): open jobs, new jobs in 7/30 days, teams hiring, leadership openings, a 0-100 hiring score and hot/warm/cold signal. Unlike company_website_enricher (tech stack and contacts) and company_team_finder (current staff), this reads open roles as a buying or growth signal. Use when you need sales triggers, recruiting leads or competitor hiring watch for a known list of companies. Do not use to discover companies from scratch (start from local_business_leads, federal_contract_finder or your own list) or for individual job search. Parameters: companies accept domains, names or direct job-board links; links are exact, names can match the wrong board. checkWebsite=true reads the careers page to find the exact board (more accurate, slower). minOpenJobs filters below-threshold companies out unbilled. titleKeywords only count matches; they do not filter. Companies with no public board are returned free with status. Returns per item: agentSummary, company, domain, signal, hiringScore, openJobs, newJobs7d, newJobs30d, leadershipJobs, leadershipTitles, topFunctions, functionCounts, remoteShare, topLocations, keywordHits, newestJobs, lastPostedAt, ats, boardUrl, matchedBy, status.
company_website_enricher: Enrich company domains from public sources (the company's own site with robots.txt respected, DNS and RDAP): name, description, published emails and phones, LinkedIn and socials, address, tech stack by category, mail provider, SaaS tools seen in DNS and domain age. Unlike company_team_finder (named people and titles) and company_hiring_signals (open jobs), this returns one firmographic row per company. Use when you have domains and need contact points, technographics or a filter like sites running Shopify or HubSpot. Do not use to find people (use company_team_finder) or to grade email security (use email_domain_security_checker). Parameters: onlyWithTech, onlyWithEmail and onlyWithPhone filter before billing, so filtered-out domains are free. extraPages (0-4) reads contact/about/team pages: more found contacts, slower runs, same price. Only published contacts are returned; no guessed emails. Unreachable sites are free. Returns per item: agentSummary, companyName, description, primaryEmail, emails, phones, linkedinUrl, socials, address, cms, techStack, techByCategory, mailProvider, emailSendingTools, verifiedServices, domainCreated, domainAgeYears, domainExpires, registrar, copyrightYear, status.
company_team_finder: Find the named people at a company from its own public website (team, leadership, about and staff pages): name, title, seniority, department, decision-maker flag, published email, LinkedIn link and the company's email pattern. Unlike company_website_enricher (one firmographic row per company) and researcher_expert_finder (academics ranked by publications), this returns one row per person; it never scrapes LinkedIn. Use when you need decision makers or staff contacts at known companies. Do not use for academic experts (use researcher_expert_finder), for company-level contacts or tech stack (use company_website_enricher), or when the site has no team page. Parameters: billing is per person, not per company, so maxPeoplePerCompany (most senior first) and decisionMakersOnly are the main cost levers; run_max_items sets maxCompanies only. Pasting the exact team page URL is faster and more reliable than a bare domain. maxPagesPerCompany trades coverage for speed. emailGuess is inferred (pattern from published emails, else unverified first.last) and comes with emailConfidence; verify before sending. Companies with no readable team page are free. Returns per item: agentSummary, company, domain, name, firstName, lastName, title, seniority, department, isDecisionMaker, email, emailGuess, emailConfidence, linkedinUrl, profileUrl, sourceUrl, foundVia.
topic_trends_tracker: Compare public interest in topics, brands, products or people over time using real Wikipedia pageview counts: daily and monthly views, 30-day and year-over-year change, peaks, spike days, a trend label and a 0-100 interest index. Unlike Google Trends (relative 0-100 only) this reports absolute views; unlike podcast_leads_finder or company_hiring_signals it measures attention, not contacts. Use when you need to size or compare interest, spot spikes, or validate a topic. Do not use for search-keyword volume or social mentions (Wikipedia attention is a proxy), or for topics without a Wikipedia article (returned free as notFound). Parameters: each topic resolves to one article in the chosen language edition; pass a Wikipedia URL to pin an ambiguous name. months sets the window (data from July 2015); year-over-year is always computed. includeDailySeries adds a dailyViews array per row and makes output much larger; leave off unless charting. Returns per item: agentSummary, topic, article, url, interestIndex, trend (surging/rising/flat/falling), totalViews, avgDailyViews, last30dViews, change30dPct, yoyChangePct, peakDate, peakViews, spikes, monthlyViews, optional dailyViews.
trucking_company_leads: Pull US and Canadian motor carrier, broker and freight-forwarder records from official FMCSA data, with phone, email, officers, fleet size, drivers, cargo, operating authority and safety rating. It runs in three modes: new USDOT registrations, filtered search of the registry, or lookup by USDOT number. Unlike local_business_leads (any category from OpenStreetMap) or npi_provider_lists (healthcare registry), this is the authoritative FMCSA registry for transportation companies. Use when you need new-entrant carrier leads (insurance, factoring, ELD, dispatch, fuel cards), carriers by lane/state/fleet/cargo, or to enrich known DOT numbers. Do not use for shipment tracking, load boards or rates. Parameters: mode=new uses daysBack and sorts newest first; mode=search ignores daysBack and uses the filters plus activeOnly; mode=lookup uses only dotNumbers. powerUnits/drivers bounds, carrierClass=forHire and requireEmail/requirePhone are the strongest narrowers and filter before billing. Phone and email are what carriers file with FMCSA and may be personal or stale. Runs that match nothing are free. Returns per item: agentSummary, dotNumber, mcNumber, legalName, dbaName, status, addedDate, daysSinceAdded, officers, phone, cellPhone, email, street, city, state, zip, powerUnits, drivers, fleetBand, cargo, hazmat, operation, carrierClasses, entityTypes, safetyRating, lastFilingDate, saferUrl.
website_change_monitor: Check a watch list of web pages against snapshots saved by your previous run and report added and removed text, change percent, price changes and keyword appear/disappear alerts, with an optional webhook when something changes. Unlike ai_search_seo_audit (one-time quality audit) and hidden_ai_instructions_scanner (concealed AI-directed text), this is stateful diffing over time. Use when you need to track competitor pricing, terms, product or careers pages on a schedule. Do not use for a one-off page read or audit (use ai_search_seo_audit), or for pages behind a login. Parameters: the first run per monitorName only saves baselines (status 'baseline saved'); reuse the same monitorName for every later run, and use a new name for a separate watch list. cssSelector, ignorePatterns and ignoreNumbersAndDates cut false alarms from banners, counters and timestamps. Below minChangePercent the old snapshot is kept, so small edits accumulate. onlyReportChanges shrinks output but every page checked is still billed; unreachable pages are free. webhookUrl posts outside the Apify run; only set it if you control that endpoint. Returns per item: agentSummary, url, label, status, changed, changePercent, addedCount, removedCount, addedLines, removedLines, prices, priceChanges, keywordsPresent, keywordsAppeared, keywordsDisappeared, titleBefore, titleAfter, previousCheckAt.
sbir_sttr_topic_radar: Find SBIR and STTR solicitation topics across agencies (DoD branches, NIH, NASA, NSF, DOE, USDA, DHS and more) by keyword, with full topic text, close dates, days left, topic numbers, official links, and DoD Q&A status and technical points of contact. Unlike grants_finder (general Grants.gov opportunities and past NIH/NSF awards) and federal_contract_finder (awarded contracts), this lists small-business R&D topics you can propose to. Use when a small business or research partner needs open SBIR/STTR topics, deadlines or a TPOC to contact. Do not use for general grants (use grants_finder) or for past contract winners (use federal_contract_finder). Parameters: empty keywords lists every topic matching the other filters, which can be large, so keep maxResults low. status=closed returns past topics to show what an agency keeps funding. includeDetails and includeDodQa each fetch extra pages per topic: richer rows, slower runs, same price; turn them off for a fast scan. Searches with no results are free. Returns per item: agentSummary, topicId, topicNumber, title, agency, branch, program, phase, status, openDate, closeDate, daysLeft, description, technicalPointOfContact, dodQaStatus, dodPublishedQuestions, officialSolicitationUrl, url.
sec_financials_excel: Return standardized annual financials for US-listed companies from SEC EDGAR XBRL 10-K data: income statement, balance sheet and cash-flow lines plus EBITDA, free cash flow, net debt, margins and growth, one row per company-year, each number tagged to its source filing. Unlike pdf_table_extractor (any PDF table, best-effort), this reads structured filings and is exact; unlike federal_contract_finder it covers public-company fundamentals, not government spend. Use when you need comps, model inputs or multi-year history for tickers or CIKs. Do not use for private companies, foreign filers without 10-Ks, quarterly data or share prices (not included). Parameters: contactEmail is required by SEC's fair-access rule and is sent only to SEC. Billing is per company-year, so worst case = companies x years; run_max_items does not set years, so cap cost with years and run_max_charge_usd. Unknown tickers are returned free with a status. Returns per item: agentSummary, company, ticker, cik, fiscalYear, periodEnd, form, filed, revenue, grossProfit, operatingIncome, netIncome, epsDiluted, operatingCashFlow, capex, freeCashFlow, ebitda, cash, totalDebt, netDebt, stockholdersEquity, margins, revenueGrowth, epsGrowth, sourceTags. The comps workbook stays in the run's Apify key-value store.
hidden_ai_instructions_scanner: Scan web pages for text hidden from people but read by AI agents (display:none, off-screen, tiny or same-color text, HTML comments, alt/meta/data attributes, zero-width and Unicode tag characters) and classify it as policy notice, manipulation or harmful prompt injection, with location and excerpt. Unlike ai_search_seo_audit (visible SEO and AI-readiness) and website_change_monitor (diffs over time), this is a security check on content an agent is about to read. Use when an agent or workflow will ingest a page and you need to know whether it carries hidden instructions, or when auditing your own site. Do not use for SEO grading (use ai_search_seo_audit) or for email security (use email_domain_security_checker). Parameters: renderJs=true runs a real browser to catch script-injected text (much slower, plus settleSecs per page); off is a fast HTTP read. agentUaDiff adds three fetches per page (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, ChatGPT-User) to detect cloaking. crawlDepth follows same-site links but maxPages always caps the run. Findings are leads for review, not proof of intent. Returns per item: page summaries (type page-summary, url, verdict, findings, categories, topSeverity, techniques, agentSummary) and findings (technique, location, excerpt, category, severity).
clinical_trial_leads: Find clinical trials on the official ClinicalTrials.gov API by condition, intervention, sponsor, phase, status and site location, with sponsor class, enrollment, dates, central contacts, principal investigators and every study site with its contacts. Unlike pubmed_evidence_table (published articles) and npi_provider_lists (all registered providers), this returns registered studies and the people and sites running them. Use when you need recruiting trials near a location, sponsor or site pipelines, or investigator and site-contact leads for CROs, suppliers or patient referral. Do not use for published results (use pubmed_evidence_table) or for funding (use grants_finder). Parameters: statuses default to recruiting and not-yet-recruiting; add COMPLETED etc. for history. countries/states/city keep trials with at least one matching site and report matchingSiteCount. updatedWithinDays suits weekly schedules. requireContact filters out uncontactable trials before billing. Searches with no results are free. Returns per item: agentSummary, nctId, title, status, phase, conditions, interventions, leadSponsor, sponsorClass, collaborators, enrollment, startDate, primaryCompletionDate, centralContactName, centralContactPhone, centralContactEmail, principalInvestigators, sites, matchingSiteCount, url.
nonprofit_leads_irs: Build nonprofit and foundation lead lists from the official IRS Exempt Organizations Business Master File, filtered by state, city, ZIP, NTEE cause, 501(c) type, public charity vs private foundation, revenue, assets and ruling year. Unlike local_business_leads (OpenStreetMap shops) and npi_provider_lists (healthcare NPI), this is the IRS EO BMF for tax-exempt orgs. Use when you need charity or foundation prospect lists for fundraising, sponsorship, grants outreach or nonprofit CRM enrichment. Do not use for for-profit businesses (use local_business_leads or company_website_enricher) or for Form 990 full-text analysis. Parameters: states is the usual starting filter; orgType any|publicCharity|privateFoundation; only501c3 defaults true; minAssets/minRevenue and sortBy=assets|revenue|newest|name rank large prospects first; maxResults caps billed rows. In-care-of and address are what the org filed with the IRS and may be a PO box or attorney. Runs that match nothing are free. Returns per item: agentSummary, ein, name, inCareOf, street, city, state, zip, nteeCode, cause, subsection, orgType, privateFoundation, rulingYear, revenue, income, assets, sizeBand, deductible, propublicaUrl, irsUrl; plus NONPROFITS_XLSX/CSV.
federal_register_monitor: Track new US federal rules, proposed rules, notices and presidential documents from the official FederalRegister.gov API, with agency, publication and effective dates, comment deadline and days left, docket IDs, RIN, abstract and comment links. Unlike grants_finder (assistance opportunities) and federal_contract_finder (awarded contracts), this monitors the Federal Register rulemaking feed. Use when compliance, policy, lobbying or capture teams need new rules or open comment periods by keyword or agency. Do not use for grant RFPs (use grants_finder) or for awarded contract data (use federal_contract_finder). Parameters: keywords and agencies narrow the search; commentsOpenOnly=true keeps only open dockets; documentTypes RULE|PRORULE|NOTICE|PRESDOCU; daysBack or publishedFrom/To set the window; significantOnly filters significant rules; maxResults caps billed documents. Empty runs are free. Returns per item: agentSummary, documentNumber, type, title, agencies, publicationDate, effectiveDate, commentsCloseDate, commentDaysLeft, commentOpen, significant, docketIds, rins, citation, abstract, commentUrl, url, pdfUrl, regulationsGovDocketUrl; plus FEDREG_XLSX/CSV.
product_recall_monitor: Pull one feed of US product recalls from openFDA (food, drug, medical device enforcement) and CPSC SaferProducts.gov (consumer products), with product, reason or hazard, recalling firm, FDA class, status, distribution, lots/UPCs, retailers and remedy. Unlike clinical_trial_leads (registered studies) and federal_register_monitor (rulemaking), this is safety recall enforcement. Use when QA, retail, insurance, marketplace or consumer-safety teams need recent recalls by keyword, firm, class, state or date. Do not use for vehicle VIN recalls (use vin_decoder_recalls) or for clinical-trial safety results. Parameters: sources food|drug|device|consumer (default all); keywords and firmContains filter before billing; classifications Class I|II|III (FDA); daysBack or dateFrom; states for distribution; maxResults caps billed recalls. Empty runs are free. Returns per item: agentSummary, source, recallNumber, date, classification, status, product, reason, firm, firmLocation, firmState, distribution, quantity, codes, retailers, remedy, hazard, url; plus RECALLS_XLSX/CSV.
vin_decoder_recalls: Bulk-decode vehicle identification numbers with the official NHTSA vPIC API and attach NHTSA recall campaigns and complaint counts for each model year in the same run (year, make, model, trim, body, engine, fuel, drivetrain, plant, safety features). Unlike product_recall_monitor (FDA/CPSC product recalls) and company_website_enricher (firmographics), this is VIN-level vehicle data. Use when dealers, fleets, insurers, marketplaces or repair shops need specs plus open safety recalls for many VINs. Do not use for consumer product or drug recalls (use product_recall_monitor) or for title/lien history. Parameters: vins (list; duplicates removed; up to 10,000); includeRecalls and includeComplaints default true; includeInvalid keeps undecodable VINs as free skipped rows; maxResults caps billed decodes. Undecodable VINs are skipped for free. Returns per item: agentSummary, vin, valid, modelYear, make, model, trim, bodyClass, vehicleType, driveType, engine, fuel, manufacturer, plant, safetyFeatures, recallCount, parkItRecall, recalls, complaintCount, nhtsaRecallUrl; plus VINS_XLSX (Vehicles + Recalls sheets)/CSV.
